title: FY25 capital plan: capacity follows demand
preview: Vertex Compute says hyperscaler demand supports a multi-year buildout and outlines a larger capital plan.
body:
Vertex Compute raised its capital plan after reporting contracted demand from cloud customers. The filing describes a multi-year buildout, but does not detail the power-delivery schedule for every announced site.

The capital plan follows contracted demand, while power-delivery timing remains a site-level variable.

title: Data-centre connection queue and reserve margin
preview: Public series shows connection requests rising while queue timing and local reserve data remain incomplete.
body:
The public series records rising connection requests alongside a tighter reserve margin in several planning zones. It is a useful baseline, but the lag means it cannot resolve the full 2028 operating-capacity question.

Connection requests are rising, but the public series does not yet resolve when queued capacity can energise.

title: Why the next campus is already spoken for
preview: An industry blog repeats the company-capex narrative and frames demand as the binding constraint.
body:
Buildout Weekly argues that demand is the binding constraint for the next wave of campuses. Its examples closely follow company announcements and add limited independent delivery evidence.

The next campus is already spoken for, according to the same demand announcements circulated by issuers.

spans.text: The next campus is already spoken for, according to the same demand announcements circulated by issuers.

title: Suppliers feel the pull of the AI buildout
preview: Supplier interviews point to strong near-term demand, but transformer and switchgear lead times are stretching.
body:
Two equipment suppliers describe a durable order book for AI infrastructure, but warn that transformers and switchgear are being booked well ahead of delivery. The reporting adds an independent check on issuer-led demand claims.

Two switchgear suppliers said booked orders now extend beyond twelve months, even as accelerator demand remains firm.

The suppliers described the order book as durable through the next two planning cycles, while cautioning that delivery dates move before revenue does.

spans.text: Two switchgear suppliers said booked orders now extend beyond twelve months, even as accelerator demand remains firm.

title: AI campuses: the equipment squeeze
preview: A short newsletter echoes Northstar’s supplier bottleneck framing with little additional sourcing.
body:
Circuit Note repeats the equipment bottleneck story and cites the same supplier comments already used in Northstar Wire. The article is useful as a duplication check, not as a second independent family.

Equipment vendors are busy and delivery windows are longer. The note cites the same public supplier comments circulated in the wire market.

spans.label: Repeated framing
spans.text: Equipment vendors are busy and delivery windows are longer. The note cites the same public supplier comments circulated in the wire market.

title: Grid connections, not chips, set the pace
preview: Interviews with grid operators and developers complicate the buildout story: interconnection studies, not chips, set the pace in constrained markets.
body:
Grid operators and developers describe a widening gap between signed connection agreements and energisation. The report argues that interconnection studies, substation work, and queue position can add years to an otherwise funded campus.

A regional grid operator told the report that a signed connection agreement is not the same as energisation; studies, substation work, and queue position can add years.

Developers in constrained markets are shifting phases or procuring behind-the-meter power, which makes announced capital spend a poor proxy for operating capacity by 2028.

spans.text: A regional grid operator told the report that a signed connection agreement is not the same as energisation; studies, substation work, and queue position can add years.

title: The interconnection queue will decide 2028
preview: A specialist report offers regional queue benchmarks and project-level interconnection lead times.
body:
GridScope Asia assembles regional queue benchmarks and project-level timelines for constrained Asian hubs. It is the most detailed source in the set, but its quote exceeds the S$1.00 per-source mandate ceiling.

The specialist dataset estimates 18–36 months from a complete interconnection application to a firm energisation window in the most constrained Asian hubs.

title: Cooling is becoming a site-selection constraint
preview: A technical review describes cooling and water requirements that can delay dense AI campuses.
body:
Technical operators report that cooling and water requirements are reshaping site selection for dense AI campuses. The review is relevant context, but it carries no project-level delivery evidence.

Cooling and water requirements can delay a dense campus even when compute equipment is available.

title: Funding the second wave of compute
preview: Debt markets remain open for strong sponsors, but construction financing is sensitive to timing and utilisation.
body:
Credit remains available to strong sponsors, although construction financing is increasingly sensitive to delivery timing and expected utilisation. The note links financing risk to operations rather than demand alone.

Construction financing is sensitive to timing and utilisation, not only to the size of the announced pipeline.

title: Specialty construction labour remains tight
preview: A public index shows specialist electrical and commissioning labour shortages across major hubs.
body:
The public index shows persistent shortages in specialist electrical and commissioning labour. Geography is broad, so it is a leading indicator rather than a project forecast.

Specialist electrical and commissioning labour remains tight across the major buildout hubs.

title: AI capex: the trillion-dollar runway
preview: A market digest compiles public company announcements and repeats the demand thesis.
body:
Market Signal Digest compiles public company announcements into a bullish runway narrative. It is a useful discovery lead but adds no independent evidence family.

The runway looks large because the digest aggregates the same public announcements across issuers.
